value.body: A storyboard artist turns a script into a sequence of drawings that show each shot (framing, camera movement and action) before production begins. Animation studios, ad agencies and film and TV production houses hire for this work, often on a project or freelance basis. A typical day involves sketching sequences, discussing them with the director and revising.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BFA, B.Des or an animation course

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Pencil and paper, digital drawing and storyboard software

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Studio staff roles and project-based freelance work

items.label: People working in AVGC (animation, VFX, gaming, comics)
items.note: Covers the whole sector; storyboard artists are a small part of it
items.source: AVGC-XR Promotion Task Force / IICT (as reported)

items.label: Animation & VFX revenue change
items.note: Linked to the Hollywood strikes and less outsourced work; the 2026 report noted ~2% growth in 2025

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most get in with a portfolio of sequential drawing: comic pages, short boards, animatics. Some begin as layout or clean-up artists in an animation studio and move into storyboarding.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Quick, clear figure and perspective drawing

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: lead storyboard artist, animation director, art director.
Freelance work is common, so income can be irregular.
A strong portfolio counts for more than the degree name.
